Shiny

Source: vignettes/shiny.Rmd
shiny.Rmd

This page is specific to R. It shows how to use the Tree View callbacks of the MUI docs, such as onSelectedItemsChange and onItemClick, in a Shiny app.

The examples need a Shiny server, so they are not run on this page: copy them into an R session to try them.

Send a value to Shiny with setInput()

Tree View callbacks are JavaScript functions. setInput(inputId, 1) creates one that sends an argument of the callback to input[[inputId]]. The 1 is the position of the argument, starting from 0: most callbacks receive the event first (position 0), then the ids (position 1).

Callback Arguments Example
onItemClick event, item id setInput("clicked", 1)
onSelectedItemsChange event, selected ids setInput("selected", 1)
onExpandedItemsChange event, expanded ids setInput("expanded", 1)
onItemFocus event, item id setInput("focused", 1)
onItemLabelChange item id, new label see Label editing

Filter a data frame with the selection

The most common use: build the tree from a data frame with asMuiTree(), and filter the data frame with the selected ids. Use levels_id so that the ids are stable and can be matched with the data frame. MUI docs

library(shiny)
library(muiMaterial)
library(muiTreeView)

to_id <- function(x) gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x))

fns <- rbind(
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Layout", fn = c("Box", "Stack", "Grid")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Inputs", fn = c("Button", "TextField", "Slider", "Switch")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Navigation", fn = c("Link", "Tabs", "Drawer")),
  data.frame(package = "muiMaterial", group = "Surfaces", fn = c("AppBar", "Toolbar", "Card")),
  data.frame(package = "muiCharts", group = "Charts", fn = c("BarChart", "LineChart", "PieChart", "Gauge")),
  data.frame(package = "muiCharts", group = "Building blocks", fn = c("ChartsContainer", "ChartsXAxis", "ChartsLegend", "Toolbar")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Routers", fn = c("RouterProvider", "createHashRouter", "createMemoryRouter")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Routes", fn = c("Route", "Outlet")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Navigation", fn = c("Link", "NavLink", "Navigate")),
  data.frame(package = "reactRouter", group = "Hooks", fn = c("useParams", "useLoaderData", "useNavigate"))
)
# Stable ids, built from the path: "Navigation", "Link" and "Toolbar" exist in two packages
fns$group_id <- paste(fns$package, to_id(fns$group), sep = "-")
fns$fn_id <- paste0(fns$package, "::", fns$fn)

fn_items <- asMuiTree(
  fns,
  levels = c("package", "group", "fn"),
  levels_id = c("package", "group_id", "fn_id")
)

ui <- muiMaterialPage(
  CssBaseline(),
  Stack(
    direction = "row",
    spacing = 2,
    sx = list(p = 2),
    Box(
      sx = list(minWidth = 280),
      RichTreeView(
        items = fn_items,
        checkboxSelection = TRUE,
        multiSelect = TRUE,
        selectionPropagation = list(descendants = TRUE, parents = TRUE),
        defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts"),
        onSelectedItemsChange = setInput("selected", 1)
      )
    ),
    Box(tableOutput("table"))
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$table <- renderTable({
    # Selecting a package or a group selects its functions, thanks to
    # selectionPropagation; keep only the rows of the selected functions.
    fns[fns$fn_id %in% input$selected, c("package", "group", "fn")]
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Track the latest item clicked

With onItemClick, Shiny receives the id of each clicked item, even if the selection doesn’t change. MUI docs

library(shiny)
library(muiTreeView)

fns <- data.frame(
  package = c("muiMaterial", "muiMaterial", "muiCharts", "muiCharts", "reactRouter", "reactRouter"),
  fn = c("Button", "Drawer", "BarChart", "PieChart", "Route", "NavLink")
)

ui <- tagList(
  RichTreeView(
    items = asMuiTree(fns),
    onItemClick = setInput("clicked", 1)
  ),
  verbatimTextOutput("clickedLabel")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$clickedLabel <- renderPrint({
    req(input$clicked)
    # Without levels_id, asMuiTree() creates ids as "<label>-<random number>":
    # remove the number to get the label back.
    gsub("-[[:digit:]]*$", "", input$clicked)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Track the expansion 

RichTreeView(
  items = fn_items,
  onExpandedItemsChange = setInput("expanded", 1)
)
# server: input$expanded contains the ids of the expanded items

React to an event with triggerEvent()

When the server only needs to know that something happened, not the value, use triggerEvent() with observeEvent():

library(shiny)
library(muiTreeView)

ui <- tagList(
  SimpleTreeView(
    onExpandedItemsChange = triggerEvent("expansionChanged"),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "muiCharts",
      label = "muiCharts",
      TreeItem(itemId = "muiCharts::BarChart", label = "BarChart()")
    ),
    TreeItem(
      itemId = "reactRouter",
      label = "reactRouter",
      TreeItem(itemId = "reactRouter::Route", label = "Route()")
    )
  ),
  verbatimTextOutput("count")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  n <- reactiveVal(0)
  observeEvent(input$expansionChanged, n(n() + 1))
  output$count <- renderText(paste("Expansion changes:", n()))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Controlled state from the server

To change the selection or the expansion from the server, render the tree on the server with renderReact() and reactOutput(), and pass the state with selectedItems or expandedItems. Keep the state in a reactiveVal() that is also updated when the user clicks on the tree. MUI docs

library(shiny)
library(muiMaterial)
library(muiTreeView)

fns <- data.frame(
  package = c("muiMaterial", "muiMaterial", "muiCharts", "muiCharts", "reactRouter", "reactRouter"),
  fn = c("Button", "Drawer", "BarChart", "PieChart", "Route", "NavLink")
)
fns$fn_id <- paste0(fns$package, "::", fns$fn)
fn_items <- asMuiTree(fns, levels = c("package", "fn"), levels_id = c("package", "fn_id"))

ui <- muiMaterialPage(
  CssBaseline(),
  Box(
    sx = list(p = 2, maxWidth = 400),
    Stack(
      direction = "row",
      spacing = 1,
      Button.shinyInput("selectCharts", "Select muiCharts", variant = "outlined"),
      Button.shinyInput("clear", "Clear", variant = "outlined")
    ),
    reactOutput("tree")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  selected <- reactiveVal(list())

  # From the user to the server
  observeEvent(input$selected, selected(input$selected), ignoreNULL = FALSE)

  # From the server to the tree
  observeEvent(input$selectCharts, {
    selected(as.list(fns$fn_id[fns$package == "muiCharts"]))
  })
  observeEvent(input$clear, selected(list()))

  output$tree <- renderReact({
    RichTreeView(
      items = fn_items,
      checkboxSelection = TRUE,
      multiSelect = TRUE,
      defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts"),
      selectedItems = selected(),
      onSelectedItemsChange = setInput("selected", 1)
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Track multiple items with checkbox selection

onItemSelectionToggle sends the id of the item that was just toggled. To keep the list of the selected items on the server, add or remove the received id. This reproduces the logic of the MUI docs. In most apps, onSelectedItemsChange, used above, is simpler.

library(shiny)
library(muiTreeView)

fns <- data.frame(
  package = c("muiMaterial", "muiMaterial", "muiCharts", "muiCharts", "reactRouter", "reactRouter"),
  fn = c("Button", "Drawer", "BarChart", "PieChart", "Route", "NavLink")
)
treeItems <- asMuiTree(fns)

ui <- tagList(
  RichTreeView(
    checkboxSelection = TRUE,
    multiSelect = TRUE,
    items = treeItems,
    defaultExpandedItems = list(treeItems[[1]]$id),
    onItemSelectionToggle = setInput("itemSelection", 1)
  ),
  verbatimTextOutput("treeLabel")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  selectedItems <- reactiveVal(character())

  observeEvent(input$itemSelection, {
    id <- input$itemSelection
    if (id %in% selectedItems()) {
      selectedItems(setdiff(selectedItems(), id))
    } else {
      selectedItems(c(selectedItems(), id))
    }
  })

  output$treeLabel <- renderPrint(gsub("-[[:digit:]]*$", "", selectedItems()))
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Security notes

  • Values sent to Shiny with setInput(), triggerEvent() or Shiny.setInputValue() come from the browser and can be forged. Restrictions such as isItemEditable or disabled items only apply to the user interface, so validate the received ids and labels on the server, for example with req(input$selected %in% fns$fn_id).
  • JS() code runs in the browser of every visitor. Only pass fixed code to it; never build the string with paste0() or glue() from user input, URL parameters, files or databases. Put the data in the items (or other arguments) and read it inside the function, e.g. getItemLabel = JS("(item) => item.name"). To embed values computed from your own data, such as a list of ids, serialize them with jsonlite::toJSON(), which escapes them, as in Rich Tree View - Items.
  • Labels given as plain strings are escaped. Never wrap untrusted text in HTML(), which is rendered as markup.
